encounters.cc: Follow-up visit after hospitalization for ischemic stroke 2 months ago to review anticoagulation plan.

lines: Follow-up visit after hospitalization for ischemic stroke 2 months ago to review anticoagulation plan.

The patient is a 72-year-old female with persistent atrial fibrillation and a history of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia complicated by ischemic stroke who returns for follow-up two months after her recent hospitalization to review her anticoagulation plan.
During that admission, she was evaluated by neurology and cardiology, and after discussion about long-term anticoagulation, she was transitioned from warfarin to dabigatran.
The change was made because she had difficulty keeping her INR in the therapeutic range despite consistent dosing and diet.
Since starting the new medication, she has noticed no bruising, bleeding gums, melena, or hematuria.
She takes her medication twice daily and has not missed any doses.
- Strangulated femoral hernia with small bowel obstruction (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
She has a history of persistent atrial fibrillation, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and stage 2 chronic kidney disease.
- Open repair of strangulated femoral hernia with small bowel resection (age 72)
Her medications include lisinopril, atorvastatin, hydrochlorothiazide, and the new anticoagulant.

- Father: Coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction at age 65

She reports she drinks an occasional glass of wine on weekends but does not use tobacco or illicit drugs.
